commit_subject: (screen-flagged) b1.6 (PR #1300): removes hard-coded exemplar entry_is_line_a..e derived rules (proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines) from every generated chapter and makes them caller inputs; summary claims runtime semantics unchanged — unsure, part of the same decoupling repair.
description: The identifiers entry_is_line_a, entry_is_line_b, entry_is_line_c, entry_is_line_d, and entry_is_line_e are caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification.

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Chapter 87's composition gated its §301/§201/§232-aluminum/§338 components on equality against five HTS lines from other chapters, so the gates were constant false for any 87xx entry and the components were dead, with proof atoms citing provisions outside this chapter.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 84 — the removed block is byte-identical to ch86's modulo the chapter prefix and the placement-variant cosmetics (this odd chapter uses 43 redundant parenthesis pairs and the `from:` spelling of the temporal lower bound instead of `effective_from:`). Same caveats as index 84: empty commit body, retained "runtime semantics are unchanged" boilerplate, re-grounding deferred to follow-up commits in PR #1300, stale exemplar paths left in module.source_verification.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to knock this down to mechanical or not_a_defect and could not: the diff deletes five whole derived rules (formula, dtype, effective `from: '2026-02-15'`, proof atoms) from the chapter-87 module, so formulas and the module's input/output surface changed (the PR's own ledger records "−500 removed exemplar-flag outputs"), which is outside the mechanical list. Each deleted rule asserted, inside a ch87 composition, that a gate fires iff `hts_number` equals a statistical reporting number from another chapter (7202.11.10.00 ferrosilicon, 7601.10.30.00 aluminum wire, 9506.62.40.40 footballs, 2203.00.00.30 beer, 8541.42.00.10 PV cells), with proof atoms citing those out-of-chapter provisions; since `schedule_base_general_rate` is `ch87_general_rate[hts_line]` and raises on a missing key, those conditions were constant-false in any evaluable ch87 entry, leaving `china_section_301_component_rate` (post lines 2993–2997), the §201 and §338 gates, and the reciprocal annex/metals exclusions dead or never excluded — a condition with no basis in this module's cited source, which is exactly untraceable_branch ("formulas grounded on the wrong provision", fix removes or re-grounds). The "not a defect, just architecture" reading fails because the pre summary already promised "Chapter and rate-line routing occur in entry preparation, never through cross-chapter RuleSpec dispatch" while the module did that routing locally, and the PR calls the same exemplar coupling one that "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins."
triage.verifier_notes:
Evidence checked: diff 085.diff (two hunks only — summary rewrite plus removal of entry_is_line_a..e), plus full pre (956a5474, 3471 lines) and post (2a6bdb01de, 3371 lines) files.

Caveats a reviewer should weigh:
1. This commit is stage one of PR #1300. The references keep the old names and the old gating: post line 2571 still has `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0 else: temporary_import_surcharge_rate`, i.e. the §122 re-gating the PR body describes ("gated on entry_is_section_122_exempt / entry_is_section_232_covered") is NOT in this module diff. So the PR's "unlawfully suppressed" line is context, not the decisive evidence for this file; the decisive evidence is the removed formulas themselves.
2. Re-grounding here is partial. The components retain out-of-chapter grounding in their own metadata, e.g. post `source: Flat ad-valorem section 232 aluminum overlay composition for HTS 7601.10.30.00` and china_301 atoms citing us/statute/hts/7202.11.10.00, and the module's source_verification still lists 2203.00.00, 7202.11.10.00, 7601.10.30.00, 8541.42.00.10, 9506.62.40.40 after the fix. A reviewer could reasonably say the untraceable grounding is only half removed at this commit.
3. The screen note's worry ("summary claims runtime semantics unchanged") is a false alarm: that sentence ("This deterministic RuleSpec serialization changes no formula tokens, dates, inputs, proof atoms, or runtime values") is boilerplate about the sibling-chapter parenthesization step and is carried verbatim from the pre summary; it is not a claim about the b1.6 flag change, which the new summary sentence describes explicitly.
4. Second-best kind considered and rejected: wrong_entity_or_scope (the gates selected the wrong population of entries). It fits loosely, but the rubric puts wrong-provision grounding and removal-type fixes under untraceable_branch, and the removed rules' proof atoms citing other chapters' HTS lines is the cleanest evidence available.
5. Confidence held at 0.7 rather than higher because the diff alone is a derived→input boundary move with byte-identical referencing formulas; the meaning change is real but its correctness depends on the caller contract stated only in the module comment ("caller inputs supplied by entry preparation from incidence classification").
